source: W3C ODRL CG formal-semantics examples C1 (C11, C12)
notes: Translated from the W3C ODRL CG formal-semantics examples (w3c/odrl@1db8e6b, folder C Evaluation of Conditions (Duties)/C1). The CG's evaluatedAction/Target/Party become the request; requestParameters describing sotw:CurrentXSDDateTime become request.at and effective_at (odrl:dateTime is the action time in due2-core). The CG reports a controlState: Inactive is Deny under its default 'close' behaviour, where due2 says NotApplicable and leaves the default to the enforcement point. Timezone-less instants are read as UTC (due2 instants are UTC, workflows §2). Upstream defect: every CG request in C1/C2 names ex:party/billie1, but the policy's assignee is ex:party/billie, and the CG's expected reports treat the request as matching (C12, C23 Permit). The translation uses ex:party/billie; read literally, every C scenario would be NotApplicable. The CG state of the world is a pay:Payment; it becomes one evidence record (actor = payer, action compensate, payAmount = netAmount). odrl:payAmount needs no binding in the policy: due2-core binds it to the witness source, so the CG's policy is used as written (due2-profiles.md §9 #6). C12's paymentDate is an untyped "2025-07-23 00:00:00"; read as 2025-07-23T00:00:00Z. Three evaluators, three readings of an unfulfilled precondition: the CG denies (C11: Inactive, Deny), FORCE activates (force-19), OVAL accepts by default (oval-duty-payment). due2 answers Pending with the duty as the route.

expected.why: ex:rule/C1 applies; its duty has no witness, which is F — outstanding (§5.3). One route: pay 5.00 EUR.
ev-pay is a compensate by the bearer (billie, inherited from the permission) before effective_at, and payAmount 5.00 = 5.00: the duty is fulfilled and the candidate is ready.
